stories.headline: Iran and Oman discuss temporary shipping lane in Strait of Hormuz
stories.body:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi in Tehran for talks about shipping [c1]. The two officials discussed an interim framework for ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz [c1].

A joint statement carried by the Oman News Agency said Iran and Oman want to establish a temporary joint maritime corridor [c2]. The two nations also plan a mine clearance project in the strait [c2].

War broke out on February 28 after the US and Israel attacked Iran [c7]. Iran blockaded the Strait of Hormuz [c7]. Washington then placed a naval counter-blockade on Iranian ports [c7]. A 60-day peace deal between Iran and the US ended in mid-August [c5].

US President Donald Trump said on social media that the US Navy cleared mines from the strait [c3]. Trump warned that any boat placing new mines will be destroyed immediately [c4]. On August 25, an unidentified projectile struck an oil tanker at the mouth of the strait [c10]. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Centre reported the attack [c10].

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced sanctions on 60 people, entities, and vessels trading with Iran [c8]. Chinese buyers take about 90% of Iranian oil exports, according to reporting by the Financial Times [c12]. China's foreign ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said China will firmly safeguard its rights [c9].

vocab.meaning: penalties applied to a country or entity

stories.headline: Canada places retaliatory tariffs up to 50% on US goods
stories.body:
Canada announced retaliatory tariffs of up to 50% on US goods starting September 8 [c13]. The new measures target $20 billion worth of American imports [c13].

The trade dispute between the two nations has grown deeper. The new Canadian tariffs will impose duties across many goods [c14]. One report said the duties cover 700 products [c14]. Another report said the counter-tariffs apply to nearly 900 items [c15]. These items equal nearly C$28 billion in value [c15]. That amount equals $20 billion [c15].

The tariffs include a 50% duty on American steel and aluminum [c14]. Canadian officials said that US steel imports to Canada have already fallen 30% [c21]. That fall happened after Canada introduced an earlier 25% tariff [c21].

The political leaders of both countries have exchanged strong statements. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney accused US President Donald Trump of wanting to destroy Canadian industries [c18]. President Trump suggested on social media that he may change the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America [c17]. Trump made the comment on Truth Social [c17].

Trump also said his administration will raise tariffs on Canadian goods in the future [c22]. He said US tariffs on Canadian vehicles, automotive parts, and steel will rise to 50% [c22]. That increase is set to start on January 1, 2027 [c22].

Trade between the two neighbours remains large. Canada maintains a trade surplus with the US of C$9.9 billion [c19]. According to Statistics Canada, that trade surplus equals $7.1 billion [c19].

To protect the domestic economy, the Canadian government announced financial aid. Canadian Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne announced an additional C$7.5 billion support package [c16]. The funds will support businesses and workers impacted by US tariffs [c16].

Canadian Industry Minister Mélanie Joly outlined details of the C$7.5 billion support package [c20]. The aid plan includes C$3 million in grants [c20]. It also includes C$2 million in interest-free loans for small businesses [c20].

an amount that is more than what is spent

stories.headline: CIA Director John Ratcliffe makes unannounced trip to Moscow
stories.body:
CIA Director John Ratcliffe made an unannounced visit to Moscow on August 25 for talks with Russian officials [c23]. CBS News first reported the trip [c23].

Tracking data from FlightRadar24 showed a US military C-17 plane left Riga at 05:50 GMT [c24]. The aircraft landed in Moscow at 07:04 GMT [c24]. It flew back to Riga shortly before 17:00 GMT on August 25 [c24]. The US Air Force Boeing C-17A Globemaster III started its journey from Joint Base Andrews in Maryland [c30]. It landed at Moscow's Vnukovo International Airport [c30].

A senior Ukrainian official told CBS News that the US notified Kyiv about the visit [c25]. The US requested Ukraine to pause strikes until the delegation left [c25]. The Financial Times reported the Trump administration asked Kyiv to pause long-range strikes on major Russian cities during the visit [c31]. But Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said no talks with US envoys were planned for the week [c29].

This trip is the first known visit by a US spy chief to Moscow since former CIA Director William Burns visited in November 2021 [c27].

vocab.meaning: a group of people chosen to represent others

stories.headline: US sanctions four Indian companies over Iranian petroleum imports
stories.body:
The United States Department of State sanctioned four Indian companies for importing Iranian petroleum products [c33]. The sanctions were issued under Operation Economic Outcast [c32]. They used Executive Orders 13846 and 13949 [c47].

The US targeted Portease Partners, Sadashiva Overseas, PP Softtech, and Prakrutees Infra Impex [c33]. Three individuals were also sanctioned [c34]. They are Portease partners Indrismiya Ashrafmiya Sheikh and Harish Ramachandra Rangi, and PP Softtech director Prashant Garg [c34].

The US Department of State said Sadashiva Overseas imported about $69 million worth of Iranian petroleum products [c35]. That trade took place between February 2024 and June 2025 [c41]. PP Softtech and Prakrutees Infra each imported about $25 million worth [c36]. PP Softtech imported products between January 2024 and June 2025 [c42]. Prakrutees Infra imported products between May 2023 and February 2026 [c43].

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the goal is to sever every economic lifeline sustaining Iran [c37]. Iranian Economy Minister Ali Madanizadeh told state television that Tehran was fully prepared for the new sanctions [c38].

stories.headline: Ajit Doval and Wang Yi hold border talks in Beijing
stories.body:
Indian National Security Advisor Ajit Doval met Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Beijing for border talks [c48]. The meeting marked the 25th round of Special Representatives talks on the India-China boundary question [c48].

Both countries discussed their long-standing border issue. India and China agreed to continue seeking a political settlement of the boundary question [c49]. They agreed to do this in the context of their overall and long-term interests [c49].

During the talks, Doval spoke about progress on local trade and travel. Doval said that the Kailash Manasarovar Yatra via Nathu La has successfully resumed [c50]. He also said that traditional border trade via all three passes has successfully resumed [c50].

Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi spoke about the broader importance of ties between the two nations. Wang said that the China-India relationship has gone beyond the bilateral scope [c51]. He said the relationship has taken on global and strategic significance [c51]. Wang also called for gradually building a positive narrative on boundary affairs between India and China [c52].

Before holding the main border talks, Doval met another senior Chinese leader. Doval held a bilateral meeting with Chinese Vice President Han Zheng in Beijing on August 25 [c53]. That meeting took place before the Special Representatives border talks [c53].

Chinese Ambassador to India Xu Feihong shared details about that meeting. Xu said that Vice President Han highlighted earlier high-level contacts between the two nations [c54]. Han highlighted meetings between Chinese President Xi Jinping and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi [c54]. Those meetings took place in Kazan and Tianjin over the past two years [c54].

vocab.meaning: an official agreement that ends a dispute

stories.headline: Student protesters clash with police in Bihar over job exams
stories.body:
Student protesters clashed with police in Patna on August 25 during a march toward the Chief Minister's residence [c56]. The march was heading toward Lok Sevak Awas, the official home of the Chief Minister [c56].

Police used batons and water cannons after protesters broke through barricades at Dak Bungalow Chowk [c57]. A Deputy Superintendent of Police was severely injured after being hit by thrown stones [c58]. Police detained at least 25 protesters in Patna before releasing them later [c67].

The protests follow a government job announcement. The Bihar government issued a notification on August 18 for 32,388 teaching posts [c59]. The posts are to be filled through the Teacher Recruitment Examination [c59]. Protesting students demanded the exam be held in a single phase without negative marks [c60].

Bihar Public Service Commission Examination Controller Rajesh Kumar Singh expressed regret over comments he made [c61]. He had quoted a Hindi proverb that students interpreted as calling them dogs [c61].

Student representatives met Bihar top bureaucrat Pratyaya Amrit [c68]. Amrit assured them of a favourable response within a couple of days [c68].
